## What it is

A 430 × 520 × 610 mm powder-coated steel mobile pedestal for the cubicle
worktops. It uses the contract-office box/box/file arrangement: two utility
drawers over one deep hanging-file drawer. Render asset, never printed.

## Design notes

The carcass starts 42 mm above the floor on four low casters whose wheels touch
z=0. A recessed toe kick, narrow folded side returns, 7 mm carcass bends, and
shallow top/side panel seams describe sheet-metal construction without softening
the cabinet into a rounded plastic box.

All three drawer faces sit 5.5 mm behind the carcass. Their 6 mm perimeter and
divider channels continue 16 mm into the body, producing real changing
occlusion. Matching near-full-width rolled pull lips sit over finger-clearance
pockets. The top utility drawer carries a modeled lock escutcheon, cylinder, and
keyway. Hidden backing keeps the scene asset one connected solid while the front
construction reads as separate manufactured panels.

## Don't

- Don't replace the drawer shadow gaps, grip pockets, or panel seams with dark
  decals; their changing occlusion is the useful detail.
- Don't restore the 18 mm all-over radius. Contract-office folded steel needs a
  restrained bend highlight and distinct panel construction.
- Don't add disconnected handles or floating casters; the full-width pull lips
  and overlapping caster forks preserve one connected render mesh.
- Don't hide the wheels by moving them deep under the carcass. Their z=0 contact
  and the recessed toe kick are what ground the pedestal.
- Don't act on printability findings; this is a scene asset.
